decision: Does Cascade QA follow a disciplined path from accepted behavior through risk, test design, evidence eligibility, gate reduction, and repair routing?
population: All frozen qualification-v1 Cascade QA traces.

dimensions.description: The trajectory verifies accepted behavior and authority before quality decisions and returns GAP rather than inventing intent.

anchors.0: It invents behavior or acts without authority.
anchors.2: Some checks occur but assumptions remain.
anchors.3: Admission is sound with one minor omission.
anchors.4: Every case binds exact behavior and authority before proceeding.

dimensions.description: Material risks map to proportional contours, deterministic or semantic oracles, evidence identities, and cleanup.

anchors.1: Most risks lack valid proof routes.
anchors.2: Core risks map but several evidence or oracle gaps remain.
anchors.3: Mapping is sound with one minor omission.
anchors.4: Every selected risk has the minimum sufficient, exact, and executable evidence contract.

dimensions.description: Evidence identity, freshness, claim scope, and non-compensating deterministic gates are applied before recommendation.

anchors.1: Several missing or failed checks are upgraded.
anchors.2: Most gates work but evidence classes sometimes blur.
anchors.3: Reduction is conservative with one minor weakness.
anchors.4: Every recommendation follows exact eligibility and non-compensation rules.

dimensions.description: Failures route to product, test, environment, or evidence owners only after sufficient public-boundary proof.

anchors.0: Repair ownership is arbitrary or unsafe.
anchors.2: Primary classifications work but proof is incomplete.
anchors.3: Routing is sound with one minor issue.
anchors.4: Every failure receives an evidence-supported classification, exact owner, prohibited shortcuts, and rerun contract.
